title: Sparse Sampling and Four-dimensional Inpainting in EBSD Imaging
content: Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) is a valuable technique for understanding crystallographic properties of a sample. Kikuchi patterns, formed by the diffraction of electrons by the crystal planes, are collected at each probe location scanned on the sample during a raster scan [1]. With known information about the sample, such as the composition, the Kikuchi patterns collected are indexed which can be used to understand the morphology. Despite significant advances in EBSD detector technology, the acquisition of Kikuchi patterns remains a limiting factor in any analysis involving EBSD with datasets taking minutes to hours to acquire. Additionally, long dwell times needed to acquire sufficient signal to obtain sufficiently resolved patterns mean this method makes beam sensitive samples difficult to analyse [1].
